data.name: Benoit
data.gender_notes: Benoit is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Benoit is derived from the Hebrew name Binyamin, which means 'son of the right hand'. In Greek and Latin, the name is translated as 'Benedictus', meaning 'blessed'. The name has been borne by several saints, including Saint Benedict of Nursia, the founder of the Benedictine order. The name Benoit carries the meaning “God's blessings” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, French, Hebrew. Parents who choose Benoit usually hope their child will grow to embody god's blessings and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.meaning: בן אויט משמעות נולד בר מזל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: בנואיט הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו בשם העברי בנימין ובנוי, שפירושו בן הימין או בנו של הגויים, נמצא בשימוש בקרב הנוצרים הצרפתים והוא מקושר לנושא של ילד בר מזל או נולד מחדש

in_greek.name: Μπενουά
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μπενουά είναι γαλλική μορφή του ονόματος Βενέδικτος που προέρχεται από το λατινικό 'benedictus', που σημαίνει ευλογημένος. Στην παράδοση των Ανατολικών Ορθοδόξων Εκκλησιών, το όνομα συνδέεται με την έννοια της ευλογίας και της αναγέννησης μέσω του βαπτίσματος

in_latin.name: Benoit
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Benoit ex gallico Benedictus derivatur, quod latine 'benedictus' seu 'beatus' significat. In primitiva Ecclesia Christiana, Benedicti nomen erat symbolum novae vitae et benedictionis divinae. Nomen hoc indicat personam quae a Deo benedicitur

in_english.name: Benoit
in_english.meaning: Benoit means blessed or good child
in_english.long_meaning: The name Benoit is of French origin, derived from the Latin name Benedictus, meaning 'blessed'. It has roots in the Hebrew name Benjamin, meaning 'son of the right hand'. Historically, the name gained popularity due to Saint Benedict, a pivotal figure in Christian monasticism. The name symbolizes a child born under good fortune or a blessing from God. In Christian tradition, Benoit/Benedict represents a person of piety, discipline, and spiritual devotion

data.cultural_impact: The name Benoit has a rich cultural heritage and has been popular in various European countries, particularly in France. It was a common name among the French nobility and was often used as a given name for boys born into privileged families. Today, the name is still widely used in France and is recognized as a masculine name with an elegant and classical sound.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Benoit has deep spiritual significance for Christians. It reminds us of the blessings and goodness of God. The name Benoit is derived from the Hebrew name Binyamin, which means 'son of the right hand'. In the Bible, this name was given to Jacob's twelfth son, and it prefigures Jesus, who is called the 'Son of God' and the 'right hand of the Father'. The name's Greek and Latin translation as Benedictus further emphasizes the spiritual meaning of the name, as it emphasizes the idea of being blessed by God. The name also has a strong connection to Saint Benedict of Nursia, who is the patron saint of Europe and is known for his wisdom, humility, and devotion to God. The name Benoit is a reminder of the spiritual blessings that come from leading a virtuous and God-centered life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Benoit, meaning "blessed" in French, symbolizes the deep spiritual connection and devotion to the divine, evoking a sense of gratitude for God's blessings and favor in one's life.

historical_references.reference: Benoit of Tours (490-575 AD) was a Christian monk and bishop who is considered the founder of the monastery at Marmoutier.
